text:
erin: quick sync9: onboarding customers reported broken correlation: node shows `x-request-id`, python logs `req_id`, and our observability dashboards can't join traces to logs. also saw raw emails in an exported span. anyone taken a look? :confused:

noah: saw it. two separate problems: naming / propagation mismatch and redaction only applied to formatted logs, not span attrs.

tasha: i propose a canonical field: `request_id` (snake_case). SDKs should copy from `x-request-id` header if present, else generate, then set in OTEL baggage + span attribute `request_id` and also bind to structured logs (structlog/threadlocal or pino/metadata).

ben: agreed on `request_id`. small node express example: 
```js
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const rid = req.headers['x-request-id'] || uuid.v4();
  req.request_id = rid;
  res.setHeader('x-request-id', rid);
  // attach to current span when available
  const span = tracer.getActiveSpan && tracer.getActiveSpan();
  if (span) span.setAttribute('request_id', rid);
  // set in OTEL baggage for downstream services
  propagation.setBaggage(createBaggageEntry('request_id', rid));
  next();
});
```

erin: nice. for python fastapi we should bind to structlog and otel baggage too. also note: our existing redaction config is a simple list in SDKs but doesn't run for OTLP exporter. we need the same rules applied pre-export.

noah: implementation idea: SDK config shape: `telemetry.redaction_rules` (regex rules + key_blocklist) and two hooks: `telemetry.pre_process_span(span)` runs when creating/modifying spans, and `telemetry.pre_export(batch)` runs just before OTLP serialization so exporters never see PII. default pre_export should apply the redaction rules to span.attributes and resource attributes.

tasha: example redaction yaml snippet: 
```yaml
telemetry:
  redaction_rules:
    - type: regex
      pattern: "(?i)[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"
      replace_with: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
    - type: key_blocklist
      keys: ["password","ssn","credit_card","api_key"]
  exporter:
    min_export_level: "info"    # don't export debug bodies by default
    capture_bodies: false
```

ben: another practical guard: enforce `min_export_level` default INFO and only export request/response bodies if `capture_bodies: true`. this avoids accidental leaks from verbose dev logs.

erin: tests: unit for SDK redactor, integration for OTLP payload asserting no PII, and an e2e sample-app showing same `request_id` across logs/traces and exported spans. add CI gate on telemetry-tests.

ops-bot: CI job telemetry-integration #204 failed: node telemetry-redaction.integration span attribute contained email.

noah: i'll add pre_export_hook to node SDK and a test that scans OTLP JSON for the email regex.

tasha: i'll do the python SDK changes + structlog sample. i'll also add a small README in sample-apps showing header exchange, baggage propagation, and how to enable `capture_bodies` for troubleshooting.

\er in: can someone draft a short RFC capturing: canonical key (`request_id`), SDK config shape (redaction_rules + pre_process_span + pre_export_hook), exporter defaults (`min_export_level`, `capture_bodies`), and testing requirements? i'll own review.

ben: i'll prepare a minimal example for the telemetry console that correlates request_id -> traces -> logs so product can demo to customers.

erin: thanks all. goal: PRs for node/python + sample-apps + RFC by EOD Thursday. :rocket:

noah: noted. i'll also add a small linter rule in telemetry-tests that fails if exporter JSON includes regex matches for the sensitive patterns.

ops-bot: Reminder: please link PRs in #devex when ready. :bell:
